5 Sample selection and descriptive statistics


We limit our sample to companies with December fiscal year-ends and obtain
60,823 company-year observations from 1987 to 2011 with nonmissing analysts’
consensus one-year-ahead and two-year-ahead annual EPS forecasts as of June. <sup>11</sup>

We require long-term growth forecasts to calculate several of the company-level
cost of equity measures, and we require actual EPS, as reported by I/B/E/S, to
estimate one of our portfolio-based cost of equity measures (i.e., Model II in
Appendix 1). In addition, following prior literature, we require earnings forecasts to
be greater for year t ? 2 than for year t ? 1 (i.e., epst?2 [ epst?1) so that we can
calculate the rOJN measure. These requirements reduce the sample to 38,378
observations. Next, we merge the I/B/E/S and Compustat data and compute our cost
of equity measures and control variables, reducing the sample to 24,072
observations. We also require data on beta and daily stock return volatility from
CRSP, which further reduces the sample to 13,044 observations. Finally, because all
